M Khaled Ahmed with Md Salim Azad, Advocates —For the Appellants.

parties:
Utu and two others ------ Convict-Appellants
vs
State ------ Respondent
full_judgment: 9. On behalf of the State, the learned Assistant Attorney-General Mr ASM Abdul Mobin and Mrs Shuchira Hossain submitted that this is a gruesome murder. On the alleged night the victim Abdul Karim went to the house of convict Azim on invitation and since then he did not return home. In the next morning his brother PW 1 went to the house of Azim to inquire about the victim who told that on the night at 11-00 PM he left the house of Azim. So, the learned Assistant Attorney-Generals submitted that admittedly the victim was last seen at the house of convict Azim and after the occurrence convict Azim along with other convicts were in absconsion. So, they submitted that their absconsion without reasonable cause leads to the presumption that they had complicity in this murder otherwise they would not have absconded but joined with the informant in search of the victim. Further, they submitted that PW 3 Abdul Kadir, who is a rickshaw-puller, saw the victim and the convicts on the road. He was coming with his rickshaw and that has been corroborated by PW 8 Ana Mia. They further submitted that admittedly there is no eye-witness of this occurrence. But the circumstances are so great and incompatible that the learned Additional Sessions Judges has rightly come to the findings that convicts Utu and Muhit out of previous enmity killed the victim in collusion with convict Azim and to that effect they managed Azim to invite the victim at his house, Further, they submitted that after the occurrence their all along absconsion has got presumptive force and the victim admittedly filed a criminal case against convicts Utu and Muhit and in that case he tried to get the convicts Utu and Muhit arrested. So, they submitted that there is strong circumstantial evidence against the convicts that they on the alleged night by inviting the victim at the house of Azim have killed him and kept his dead body on the pathway of the tea garden. So, the learned Assistant Attorney-Generals submitted that the learned Additional Sessions Judge has rightly convicted the appellants and in this appeal there is nothing to interfere with.
